content: 1. The effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. It is recommended to use a non-hormonal contraceptive method. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Ethinylestradiol can increase the levels or effects of dasatinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Deferasirox can decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Demeclocycline may reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of desipramine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. Oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) may be decreased by ethinylestradiol, potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of TCA-related adverse effects. 6. Dexamethasone can decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 7. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Dicloxacillin may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of dosulepin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. Oxidative metabolism of TCAs may be decreased by ethinylestradiol, potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of TCA-related adverse effects. 10. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of doxepin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. Oxidative metabolism of TCAs may be decreased by ethinylestradiol, potentially leading to increased serum concentrations of antidepressants and a higher risk of TCA-related adverse effects. 11. Doxycycline may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 13. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of duloxetine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Efavirenz can decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 15. Elafibranor may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elafibranor, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce systemic exposure to hormonal contraceptives. Switch to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during elafibranor treatment and for at least three weeks after the last dose. Monitor closely. 16. Elagolix decreases the levels of norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered. Ethinylestradiol levels may also be decreased by elagolix. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of elagolix by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Estrogen-containing contraceptives are expected to reduce elagolix efficacy. The effects of progestin-only contraceptives on elagolix efficacy are unknown. Advise women to use non-hormonal contraceptives during elagolix treatment and for one week after discontinuing elagolix. 18. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Elvitegravir may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative non-hormonal methods of contraception to replace combination oral contraceptives. 20. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases levels of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Enasidenib may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of enasidenib with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates, as minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. 22. Encorafenib may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Encorafenib may also decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may lose efficacy when co-administered with encorafenib. Since encorafenib can cause fetal harm, advise women of childbearing potential to use highly effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 23. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of enoxaparin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 24. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when co-administered with enzalutamide. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia. 25. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of eplerenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely. 26. Erythromycin base may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 27. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 29. Erythromycin stearate may decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may decrease hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 30. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use additional or alternative non-hormonal birth control methods. 31. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of exemestane by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exemestane should not be given concurrently with any estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 33. Oral contraceptives may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Exenatide may slow gastric emptying, reducing the extent and rate of absorption of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide. Monitor closely. 34. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of fedratinib with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors, as the effects of such combinations have not been studied. 36. Felbamate decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. 38. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Fezolinetant's AUC and peak plasma concentration are increased when co-administered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 39. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 40. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased flibanserin adverse effects may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Fosamprenavir may decrease the AUC of amprenavir and lead to a loss of virologic response. Co-administration with ethinylestradiol may alter hormone levels. Alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 44. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when co-administered with fosphenytoin. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, and menorrhagia. 45. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates when co-administered with fostemsavir. Do not exceed an ethinylestradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 46. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of frovatriptan by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 47. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely.
